name: Caravan
description: Reliable prediction of river floods in the first 72 hours can reduce harm because emergency agencies have sufficient time to prepare and deploy for help at the scene. Such river flood prediction models already exist and perform relatively well in most high-income countries. But, due to the limited availability of data, these models are lacking in low-income countries. Here, we offer the first global river flood prediction framework based on the newly published Caravan dataset. Our framework aims to serve as a benchmark for future global river flood prediction research. To support generalizability claims we include custom data evaluation splits. Further, we propose and evaluate a novel two-path LSTM architecture (2P-LSTM) against three baseline models. Finally, we evaluate the generated models on different locations in Africa and Asia that were not part of the Caravan dataset.
evaluation_method: forecast error metrics (e.g. RMSE/MAE and flood prediction skill scores)
reputation: A notable global flood forecasting benchmark built on the Caravan dataset, used to study generalization across regions and low-data settings.
notes: Non-LLM geoscience benchmark; results depend strongly on geographic split and data availability, with emphasis on out-of-distribution generalization.
